official_title.value: TO REQUIRE VOTERS TO PRESENT PHOTO IDENTIFICATION IN ORDER TO VOTE

full_text.value:
Proposed Constitutional Amendment
TO REQUIRE VOTERS TO PRESENT PHOTO IDENTIFICATION IN ORDER TO VOTE
Proposed by Joint Resolution of the General Assembly
To enact Section 5 of Article V of the Constitution of the State of Ohio
A majority yes vote is required for the adoption of Section 5.
This proposed amendment would:
• Require voters to present an approved form of government-issued photo identification in order to vote.
• Allow state law to provide for an alternative method of verifying a voter's identity for a voter who has a sincere religious objection to being photographed and, therefore, does not possess an approved form of government-issued photo identification.
• Require that voters who do not vote in person provide an approved form of government-issued photo identification, unless the law authorizes those persons to vote by providing a signature and at least one other specified unique identifier.
• Define approved forms of government-issued photo identification as an unexpired Ohio driver license or state identification card; a United States passport or passport card; or a United States military identification card, Ohio National Guard identification card, or United States Department of Veterans Affairs identification card.
If approved, the amendment shall take effect immediately.
A "YES" vote means approval of the amendment.
A "NO" vote means disapproval of the amendment.
SHALL THE AMENDMENT BE APPROVED?

placed_by.detail: Proposed by Joint Resolution of the General Assembly (Substitute Senate Joint Resolution 10, 136th General Assembly); adopted by the Senate 6-3-2026 and by the House 6-10-2026

That county document carries the header "Please note that the language below is only a summary" for the whole list; the State Issue 3 block matches the Ballot Board ballot-language structure, but a human should check it against the SOS certified ballot language once reachable. Line breaks and bullet characters are reflowed from the PDF layout.

official_summary: the Ballot Board also adopts an "explanation" of the amendment, published in the SOS Issue 3 report, which is blocked (403). The ballot language is the ballot text and the official arguments for/against are not neutral, so the summary is left null. (The Legislative Service Commission bill analysis of Sub. S.J.R. 10 exists on the legislature site but is a bill analysis, not a voter summary.)
full_text.url: the enrolled text of Sub. S.J.R. 10 on the Ohio Legislature site (the full amendment text).
opposition_committee_name / opposition_website: Ohio campaign-finance filings are on ohiosos.gov, which is blocked (403); no committee could be verified from an official filing.
proponent_website: no official filing reachable (ohiosos.gov blocked).

party_positions: the Ohio Democratic Party site (ohiodems.org) has an op-ed by the party chair criticising the amendment as unnecessary, but no explicit published position (e.g. "vote no") was found, so no Democratic Party entry is recorded. No other party position was found.

legislative_vote: Senate adoption 6-3-2026 (22-9) and House adoption 6-10-2026 (62-30) from the Ohio Legislature votes page, which lists each member with party. "other" = members not recorded (Senate 33 seats, House 99 seats; vacancies not checked). One Republican (Sen. Al Cutrona) voted no in the Senate.
